newsitem.title: ITALY: Italy coalition partners meet on mini-budget.
newsitem.headline: Italy coalition partners meet on mini-budget.

text.p: Prime Minister Romano Prodi began a meeting with representatives of parties that support his coalition on Wednesday to discuss the cost-cutting mini-budget.
Among the leaders attending the meeting was Fausto Bertinotti, whose Communist Refoundation party is a key government ally although it has no ministers in the cabinet.
Bertinotti is opposed to social spending cuts and taxes.
Among others attending the meeting were Massimo D'Alema, head of the Democratic Party of the Left, the largest party in Prodi's coalition, and Treasury Minister Carlo Azeglio Ciampi.
The cabinet is due to discuss the mini-budget on Thursday morning and Prodi has said it will be ready before Easter.
The package is expected to include some 15.5 trillion lire of deficit-cutting measures aimed at priming the economy for the single European currency.
Prodi discussed the mini-budget with the head of Italy's employers association Confindustria on Tuesday evening and was due to meet union leaders later on Wednesday. --Rome newsroom +396-6782501
